game_identity_and_current_behavior.core_player_goal: keep the health meter alive by dragging bug entities away from the giant foot before they linger too long
game_identity_and_current_behavior.core_verb: grab and drag bugs away from their spawn positions until they are cleared
game_identity_and_current_behavior.fail_state: health drains to zero after bugs remain on the foot long enough
game_identity_and_current_behavior.success_or_score_state: score increases by 100 per cleared bug and the HUD reports cumulative clears
game_identity_and_current_behavior.camera_viewport_assumptions: single full-screen portrait-friendly canvas with DOM overlays, no scrolling camera, play centered on a large foot in the lower-middle playfield
game_identity_and_current_behavior.input_model: mouse and touch drag input; tap/press selects a nearby bug, pointer movement repositions it, release clears if dragged beyond a distance threshold
moment_to_moment_loop: spawn bugs within an elliptical area over the foot
player grabs the nearest bug under the pointer
dragged bugs visually lift and rotate
releasing a bug after sufficient displacement removes it and restores some health
uncleared bugs age in place and eventually damage health continuously
spawn cadence accelerates gradually as difficulty rises
game_identity_and_current_behavior.existing_progression: no explicit levels; there is continuous survival escalation through faster spawning and pressure accumulation

mechanic_decomposition.notes: core play identity; do not alter thresholds or gesture semantics unless a tiny repair is required

mechanic_decomposition.description: bugs mostly idle in place with procedural wobble; dragged bugs follow pointer and gain lift/rotation
mechanic_decomposition.notes: visual feel is tied to bug entity update logic and should remain intact

mechanic_decomposition.description: entities spawn inside a bounded ellipse; spawn interval decreases as difficulty rises over time
mechanic_decomposition.notes: safe to reinterpret visually as themed incursions, but cadence math should remain unchanged in this stage

mechanic_decomposition.description: selection uses radial proximity to pointer; clear resolves through drag-distance threshold rather than physics collision
mechanic_decomposition.notes: this is the real interaction model and should not be replaced with tapping, swiping lanes, or hitboxes

mechanic_decomposition.description: each cleared bug grants 100 score and the HUD displays rounded clear count text
mechanic_decomposition.notes: keep semantics exactly; only wording and framing may change

mechanic_decomposition.description: bugs that remain too long begin draining health, triggering warning flash and danger reaction messaging at low health
mechanic_decomposition.notes: do not change damage logic or fail semantics

mechanic_decomposition.description: successful removal restores health and spawns celebratory particles
mechanic_decomposition.notes: reward framing, particle identity, and copy can shift to the remix theme

mechanic_decomposition.description: start screen, active run, and game-over screen are DOM overlays around one survival loop
mechanic_decomposition.notes: screen copy, framing, and visual worldbuilding are safe theming surfaces

mechanic_decomposition.description: top HUD shows health bar and clear count; reaction cards show success and danger callouts
mechanic_decomposition.notes: labels, iconography, colors, and fictional framing can change safely

complexity_profile.honest_assessment: The source game is mechanically narrow but readable: one input verb, one hazard type, one pressure loop, and one escalating spawn variable. Its complexity comes from increasingly dense timing and prioritization rather than from multiple subsystems.
what_more_complex_should_mean_safely: clearer level fiction layered over the same survival loop
stronger world progression across five thematic stages
more readable hazard/reward language using Harry Potter motifs
graduated UI messaging that frames each run segment as a magical containment exam
visual escalation in background, props, particles, and bug styling
optional reuse of the existing difficulty ramp as the backbone for conceptual levels
avoid_for_complexity: rewriting the drag mechanic into spell-casting buttons
adding combat, mana, lane systems, or projectile logic
changing score, health, or failure semantics
altering the main loop, collision model, or spawn architecture

protected_mechanics: single-screen canvas playfield centered on the foot target area
health drain from uncleared entities after linger time
safe_theming_surfaces: title, labels, instructional copy, and failure text
procedural canvas art for the foot, bugs, tweezers, particles, and auras
background gradients, ambient overlays, and animated magical scenery
reaction card imagery and callout phrasing
fictional identity of the bug entities and the removal tool
audio source mapping if later stages add approved remote media

remix_premise.high_concept: The player is a Hogwarts groundskeeper-magizoology trainee clearing enchanted Cornish pixie infestations and cursed critters from a giant magical footprint in a castle training chamber before chaos overwhelms the ward.
why_it_fits: dragging pests away naturally maps to magical creature containment without changing controls
the giant foot/grounded stage can be reframed as a bewitched bootprint, giant footprint, or enchanted training target
bugs can become pixies, cursed beetles, or dark magical pests with strong procedural silhouettes
five levels can represent a journey through Hogwarts spaces and escalating magical mishaps
recognizable_elements: spell-glow colors and wandlike light trails
owlery, greenhouse, corridor, forbidden forest, and final dark chamber settings
magical containment language instead of bug-cleaning language
remix_premise.world_premise: A practical Defense Against the Dark Arts clean-up drill spirals into a castle-wide magical pest outbreak. The player uses enchanted tongs/levitation tongs to flick creatures off an unstable footprint sigil and keep the ward meter charged.

level_1.title: Hogwarts Boot Room
level_1.definition: Base transformed experience. The player learns they are clearing escaped pixies and cursed beetles from an enchanted bootprint training mat in a warmly lit Hogwarts utility room.
level_1.proof_of_scale: Uses current spawn behavior and drag semantics unchanged while reskinning HUD as a ward meter and clears as captures.

level_1_5.title: Moving Stair Mischief
level_1_5.definition: First meaningful escalation. The same mechanics remain, but the backdrop becomes a shifting staircase corridor, danger feedback becomes more urgent, and creature variants gain stronger magical glow/readability.
level_1_5.proof_of_scale: Demonstrates that progression can come from atmosphere, creature interpretation, callout language, and pressure framing before any risky logic changes.

five_level_difficulty_progression.title: Boot Room Induction
five_level_difficulty_progression.player_facing_goal: Keep the practice ward stable by removing escaped pixies from the enchanted footprint.
five_level_difficulty_progression.difficulty_intent: Most readable introduction to the drag-and-clear loop.
five_level_difficulty_progression.safe_mechanics_knobs: Use existing early-run spawn pace only; no logic changes required.
five_level_difficulty_progression.hazard_reward_interpretation: Hazards are mischievous pixies; rewards are tidy captures and ward stabilization.
five_level_difficulty_progression.failure_risk_to_watch: Overcomplicating the first screen with too much franchise clutter.
five_level_difficulty_progression.visual_progression_beat: Warm amber storage room with floating trunks, scarves, and candle motes.

five_level_difficulty_progression.title: Moving Stair Mischief
five_level_difficulty_progression.player_facing_goal: Contain corridor pests before the staircase ward collapses.
five_level_difficulty_progression.difficulty_intent: Same loop, but with a clearer sense of urgency and denser magical motion.
five_level_difficulty_progression.safe_mechanics_knobs: Allow the native ramp to reach moderate pressure; keep systems unchanged.
five_level_difficulty_progression.hazard_reward_interpretation: Pixies and cursed scarabs clutter a shifting corridor landing.
five_level_difficulty_progression.failure_risk_to_watch: Ambient staircase motion implying actual moving platforms or new hazards.
five_level_difficulty_progression.visual_progression_beat: Portrait hall and stair silhouettes subtly sliding in the background.

five_level_difficulty_progression.title: Greenhouse Overflow
five_level_difficulty_progression.player_facing_goal: Stop magical pests from swarming the greenhouse sigil before the roots lose containment.
five_level_difficulty_progression.difficulty_intent: Represents the full intended stack: readable chaos, stronger particles, fuller thematic identity.
five_level_difficulty_progression.safe_mechanics_knobs: Mid-run native spawn cadence and warning feedback become the main challenge.
five_level_difficulty_progression.hazard_reward_interpretation: Mandrake mites and venomous beetles are removed from a glowing soil print.
five_level_difficulty_progression.failure_risk_to_watch: Plant decoration obscuring entities against the playfield.
five_level_difficulty_progression.visual_progression_beat: Glasshouse panes, vines, drifting spores, and greener magical highlights.

five_level_difficulty_progression.title: Forbidden Forest Edge
five_level_difficulty_progression.player_facing_goal: Hold the protective ward as darker creatures breach the forest boundary.
five_level_difficulty_progression.difficulty_intent: Same full stack under more pressure and moodier readability tension.
five_level_difficulty_progression.safe_mechanics_knobs: Later-run spawn pressure, danger callouts, and lower-health moments do the work.
five_level_difficulty_progression.hazard_reward_interpretation: Shadow pixies and cursed beetles become a nighttime incursion at the forest line.
five_level_difficulty_progression.failure_risk_to_watch: Dark palette reducing contrast for draggable enemies.
five_level_difficulty_progression.visual_progression_beat: Moonlit trees, blue mist, spiderweb filaments, and stronger magical warning glows.

five_level_difficulty_progression.title: Battle of the Clock Tower
five_level_difficulty_progression.player_facing_goal: Maintain the final defense sigil during a castle-wide magical outbreak.
five_level_difficulty_progression.difficulty_intent: Upper readable pressure while preserving clarity and control reliability.
five_level_difficulty_progression.safe_mechanics_knobs: Native late-run spawn density only; no extra mechanic layers.
five_level_difficulty_progression.hazard_reward_interpretation: The same pests are now framed as a final cursed swarm during an emergency lockdown.
five_level_difficulty_progression.failure_risk_to_watch: Turning finale spectacle into visual clutter that hides bugs or the pointer tool.
five_level_difficulty_progression.visual_progression_beat: Storm-lit tower windows, lightning pulses, house-banner accents, and heightened ward energy.

mechanics_ranking_top_5.reasoning: The remixed result remains a direct-manipulation cleanup game where threats are removed from a contaminated area.
Successful dragging and clearing produces an immediate tactile relief loop.
Low-to-mid pressure runs can feel soothing visually, though the timer pressure keeps it from being truly relaxing.
The player is pressured by increasing pace, but movement is not runner-like.
Escalating spawns create a defense flavor, though the mechanics remain cleanup-centric rather than combat-centric.

identity_summary.objective: protect a magical ward by removing enchanted pests before they destabilize it
identity_summary.progression: five themed Hogwarts worlds expressed through escalating presentation and native survival pressure
identity_summary.likely_audience: casual mobile players, Harry Potter fans, arcade cleanup game players
